isolation_note: Adapted Pi subprocess orchestration provides a distinct process, no-session child, and fresh model context. The child shares the project filesystem and inherits the parent environment/credentials; it is not a filesystem or credential sandbox. Ambient extensions are disabled, so a model registered only by a custom-provider extension is unavailable.
FIDELITY: On Pi, the parent remains the Orchestrator and model-callable delegation runs a separate ephemeral Pi process with isolated process, session, and model context. Filesystem and credential isolation are NOT provided. Ambient extensions are disabled in children, so models supplied only by a custom-provider extension are unavailable and delegation fails closed. block-dangerous and protect-sensitive are bounded NATIVE gates for their declared literal patterns. enforce-lease is ADAPTED/PARTIAL: structured write/edit and supported shell redirection/tee targets are checked against both role and task scopes, but other shell write mechanisms are unsupported. budget is ADVISORY: child reports are bounded self-reports, not a computed gate. format/typecheck are ADVISORY instructions only. EMPTY-SCOPE (UNSCOPED) ROLES FAIL CLOSED: one or more roles carry an empty write_scope (read-only roles, e.g. code-reviewer); having no per-path scope, they are UNSCOPED, so the lease gate BLOCKS every write/edit before it runs (an unscoped role cannot write). This is enforcement (fail-closed), NOT an unenforced gap and NOT a silent allow.

enforce-lease.mechanism: ADAPTED/PARTIAL generated Pi child-process tool_call gate: structured write/edit targets and supported literal shell redirection/tee targets are project-normalized, checked through existing symlink components, matched against both the canonical role write_scope and the latest human-gate-approved delegation taskWriteScope (their intersection), and hard-blocked before execution when off-scope. The persistent parent Orchestrator excludes and hard-blocks bash/write/edit. Empty task/role scopes, malformed supported targets, absolute/traversal escapes, and symlink escapes fail closed. This is not comprehensive shell-write enforcement: touch, cp, mv, install, sed -i, interpreters, build tools, shell expansion, and other unsupported command forms are not extracted and must not be claimed as lease-gated.

block-dangerous.mechanism: Bounded native Pi tool_call gate: bash commands matching the declared dangerous-command regex corpus are hard-blocked before execution, while tested benign controls are allowed. This claim covers those literal matcher forms only; it does not claim sound arbitrary-shell parsing, quote concatenation, expansion, or command normalization.

protect-sensitive.mechanism: Bounded native Pi tool_call gate: declared sensitive structured path fields and ordinary literal shell tokens such as cat .env, cat .npmrc, and .ssh/config are hard-blocked before execution. Missing built-in path inputs, malformed shell quoting/substitution, non-string bash commands, and token overflow fail closed. Unknown custom tool schemas are explicitly outside this claim; the tokenizer does not expand variables or claim sound arbitrary-shell interpretation.

format.mechanism: .pi/SYSTEM.md + per-role prompt instruction block only, clearly labelled "ADVISORY — NOT ENFORCED ON PI (instruction only)": Pi's on("tool_call") gate blocks but does not run post-edit formatters, and the IR carries no per-language formatter command, so formatting is NOT enforced. The agent is instructed to format edited files. Making this native needs IR-enrichment (per-language formatter command) deferred this cycle.

typecheck.mechanism: .pi/SYSTEM.md + per-role prompt instruction block only, clearly labelled "ADVISORY — NOT ENFORCED ON PI (instruction only)": Pi has no post-edit type-check hook the compiler can wire deterministically, and the IR carries no per-language checker command, so type-checking is NOT enforced. The agent is instructed to type-check edited files. Making this native needs IR-enrichment deferred this cycle.

budget.mechanism: ADVISORY only: each isolated specialist must return one schema-bounded completion report whose self-reported file/line totals are checked against the delegated budget. Pi/System2 does not compute those totals from the repository diff, so the report is evidence for parent verification, not a native budget gate.
